Members of the public wishing to make public comment may do so in one of the following
ways:

(1) By directly addressing the Planning Commission in person at the time(s) allotted on the agenda
for such comment. Persons wishing to address the Planning Commission in person are asked to
fill out a speaker card providing their name and indicating whether they wish to address the Planning
Commission on an item(s) of business appearing under (i) the Public Hearing portion of the agenda;
(ii) any item of business appearing under any other portion of the agenda; and/or (iii) a non-
agendized matter that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Planning Commission. Speaker
cards should be submitted to City Staff prior to the Planning Commission’s approval of the agenda,
if possible; or

(2) Email or Telephone – All interested parties can submit comments in advance to the Planning
Division’s general email at planning@elmonteca.gov or by calling the City’s telephone line: (626)
258-8626. All comments must be received by the Planning Division no later than 3:00 pm on
September 23, 2025.

8.  Design Review (DR) No. 07-23 and Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 12-23

  Address/Location: 12432 Valley Boulevard / APNs: 8109-013-014 and 8109-013-015

  Request:  The original project involved demolition of two (2) existing commercial
  buildings and the development of a 58,955 square foot, four-story hotel
  with a subterranean level parking garage on an approximately 1.39-acre
  site. The project site consisted of merger of two parcels and the vacation
  of Rumford Avenue, a dead end street along the westerly side of the
  project site, to allow the development of a four (4) story, 52.5-foot tall
  hotel with 97 guest rooms, a total of 97 parking spaces, and amenity
  spaces for use by hotel guests and employees including a lobby, office,
  swimming pool, gym, and a small eating area (1,285 sf).

  The Applicant now requests DR No. 07-23 and CUP No. 12-23 to revise
  the original project by no longer seeking the vacation and acquisition of
  Rumford Avenue and, thereby, reducing the overall allowable size and
  scale of the hotel development on an approximately 1.045-acre site in
  the C-3 (General Commercial) zone. The proposed project proposes to
  allow the development and operation of a 45,483-square-foot, three (3)
  story, 42.5-foot-tall hotel with 90 guest rooms, a total of 90 on-site parking
  spaces located in the subterranean garage and at-grade, and amenity
  spaces for use by hotel guests and employees including a lobby, office,
  swimming pool, gym, and a small eating area. This request is made
  pursuant to Chapter 17.123 (Conditional and Minor Use Permits) and
  Chapter 17.122 (Design and Minor Design Review) of the El Monte
  Municipal Code (EMMC).

  CEQA Recommendation:
  Pursuant to CEQA Guidelines, an Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration (IS/MND) was
  adopted for the original project in June 2018. An Addendum to the adopted IS/MND was
  prepared for the revised project. The Addendum substantiates that the analysis presented
  in the adopted IS/MND is sufficient to satisfy the environmental analysis for the revised
  project, and that with incorporation of the mitigation measures that were previously
  identified, the revised project would not result in any significant new, additional, substantially
  different, or substantially increased environmental impacts than were previously evaluated.
  The Addendum demonstrates through its impact analysis that the revised project does not

  Planning Commission Agenda | 3

  General explanation of how the meeting is conducted:
  1. The staff report is presented by City Planning staff.
  2. The City Planning Commissioners ask questions if necessary for clarification.
  3. The City Planning Commission Chair opens the public hearing.
  4. The applicant makes a presentation to the City Planning Commission.
  5. Individuals speaking in favor of the project address the Commission.
  6. Individuals speaking against the project address the Commission.
  7. The applicant responds to project opponents.
  8. The public hearing is closed.
  9. City Planning Commission members discuss the project.
  10. City Planning Commission members vote on the project.
  11. Any interested party who disagrees with the City Planning Commission decision may appeal the Commission’s
  decision to the City Council within 10 calendar days of the adoption of the resolution. Any appeal filed must be
  directed to the City Clerk’s Office and must be accompanied by a fee of $3,546.00. Any individual that received
  notice of this meeting from the City of El Monte will receive notice of an appeal, if one is filed.

  ACTION MINUTES FOR THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING HELD ON

Let the record reflect that Director Fowler addressed the Commission at this point to advise that
the Commissioners elect an Interim Chairperson and Interim Vice Chairperson temporarily until
the Commission is comprised of all seven members accordingly on a meeting-by-meeting
basis.

Commissioner Tamashiro advised his fellow Commissioners that prior to the new term he
served as Chairperson and Commissioner Salas served as Vice-Chair. With no objection he
suggested that for this first meeting he serve as Interim Chair and Commissioner Salas
serve as Vice-Chair for this meeting so that the new Commissioners can observe how the
meetings are typically done.

appoint Commissioner Salas as Vice-Chairperson for the 9-9-2025 meeting.

Motion carried 4 – 0

8. Time Extension (EXT) No. 20-2025

Address/Location: 10561 Santa Fe Drive / 8578-022-002

Request: The applicant has submitted a Time Extension request for a previously approved
project consisting of Design Review (DR) No. 12-22 to construct a five-story, 212-unit apartment
complex at 10561 Santa Fe Drive.

City Planner Elias provided a PowerPoint presentation.

The Commissioners discussed: the length of plans and CA Building Codes.

City Planner Elias responded to the question regarding the length of plans and confirmed that
during plan check the plans are valid for 12 months. In addition, during the plan check
process, applicants have a certain window in which they can pull permits unless an extension
is granted by the Building and Safety Division. At this point it was determined that the plans
need to be updated per the City’s current code.

Public Comment:

None.

Motion: Following the discussion, it was moved by Interim Chair Tamashiro to approve the
request for a one (1) year Time Extension; seconded by Commissioner Moreno.

Motion carried 4 – 0

9. Consideration of Name for future Community Park

Address/Location: 4045 Gilman Road / APN 8549-004-900

Request: Approval to formally designate a name for the future community park located at 4045
Gilman Road.

  September 9, 2025 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES | 2
 Community & Economic Development Director Fowler provided a PowerPoint presentation.

The Commissioners discussed: opportunities to get feedback from the community for the
naming of parks, support of Hilda L. Solis for the project and the El Monte community, history
of Maclaren hall, lack of facilities to name, when is the groundbreaking for the future park, two
emails received regarding other name suggestions for the future park, lack of community
engagement, confusion regarding existing Hilda L. Solis Park in Baldwin Park, alternatives to
add to the proposed name to divert confusion from existing Hilda L. Solis Park, the different
type of facilities named after Hilda Solis, and implementing more community outreach moving
forward during the naming process.

Director Fowler responded to the comments regarding opportunities to get feedback from the
community for the naming of parks and reported that originally the name for this future park
would have been Maclaren Park. However, due to the issues behind the facility, the
Community and Economic Development Department felt that due to the support that has been
received by Supervisor Solis, and the funding involved from the County to develop the park,
they serve as reasons to justify the proposed park name of Hilda L. Solis Community Park.

Director Fowler also reported that for some of the other parks that are being developed right
now, there is community outreach being done to determine the type of amenities the
community would like for the respective proposed park project. In this case, the County is
close to a groundbreaking, therefore, the City would like to have a name for the park prior to
the groundbreaking.

Director Fowler responded to the question regarding the date of the groundbreaking and
confirmed that the project site has planned demolition for the fourth quarter to remove the
buildings. The City has tentatively planned a groundbreaking for the fourth quarter of this year
or the first quarter of next year subject to the timeline of the demolition.

Director Fowler responded to the concern regarding lack of community engagement and
reported that the City took the naming of the park as an opportunity to honor Supervisor Solis
who has championed the park. Per the City’s guidelines for the naming of facilities, the
proposed name of “Hilda L. Solis Community Park” hit all the criteria needed for a proposed
name. In addition, the proposed site being a County property, and as she is a County
Supervisor, the City felt this was a great opportunity for the proposed name of the future park.
There was community outreach done prior to determine the type of amenities the community
wanted to see at this park and at those meetings there was no suggestion for the naming of
the park. In addition, since this project is a collaborative effort between the City and the LA
County, the City felt at this time that the name should reflect and memorialize the support
provided by Supervisor Solis.

Director Fowler responded to the concern regarding the existing Hilda L. Solis Park in Baldwin
Park and reported that this issue was considered when suggesting the name for this future
park.

Director Fowler responded to the comment regarding different alternatives to add to the
proposed name to divert confusion from existing Hilda L. Solis Park and reported that they
can have a discussion with staff.
  September 9, 2025 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES | 3
 Public Comment:

None.

Motion: Following the discussion, it was moved by Interim Vice-Chair Salas to adopt a resolution
no. 3689 recommending City Council approval to formally designate a name: Hilda L. Solis
Community Park for the future community park located at 4045 Gilman Road; seconded by
Commissioner Moreno.

Motion carried 4 – 0

10. Director’s Report:

Director Fowler brought to the attention of the Commissioner the need for an election to appoint
a Planning Commission Chair & Vice-Chair. As stated earlier, the meetings would be comprised
of an Interim Chair and Chairperson until all the Commissioner seats are appointed by Distrct. In
addition, the term would be similar as January to January. However, for the purpose of the
remaining year, the elected Chair and Vice-Chair would serve through the end of this year.

Interim Chair Tamashiro suggested that the Interim status remain the same for all meetings
moving forward until an election is needed once all seven Commissioners are appointed to the
Commission as to save time to not need to appoint an Interim Chair and Vice-Chair for all
meetings moving forward.

Director Fowler reported that a special Zoning Review Committee Meeting will be held September
23rd. City Planner Elias added that the applicant has been waiting to move forward their project,
therefore, a special meeting will be held to review the proposed project.

City Planner Elias provided brief background on the purpose of the Zoning Review Committee to
the new members of the Commission.

Commissioner Covarrubias volunteered to be appointed as the Zoning Review Planning
Commissioner Committee member and Interim Chair Tamashiro will continue as the alternate.

Motion: Following the discussion, it was moved by Interim Chair Tamashiro to appoint
Commissioner Covarrubias as the Zoning Review Committee member and Interim Chair
Tamashiro will continue as the alternate ; seconded by Interim Vice-Chair Salas.

Motion carried 4 – 0

Lastly, Director Fowler reported that there will be a Planning Commissioners training at the next
Planning Commission meeting, which will go over the function of the Planning Commission
meeting and the roles and responsibilities. In addition, the Commission members will be provided
a radius map to confirm projects in their respective district.

11. City Attorney’s Report

None.
  September 9, 2025 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES | 4
 12. Commissioner Comments:

Interim Vice-Chair Salas welcomed the new Planning Commissioners. In addition, asked that
during the time the Planning Commission did not meet did projects get held back due to time.

City Planner Elias confirmed that there were no projects that were pressing to come before the
Commission. There will be projects presented at the upcoming meetings.

Interim Vice-Chair Salas asked about the status of the project on Peck Rd in regards to the In-N-
Out, Raising Canes, and Starbucks project.

City Planner Elias responded to the question regarding the status of the project on Peck Rd and
confirmed that a representative from Raising Canes reached out and confirmed that they will
begin plan check on Wednesday 9-10-25. The efforts for demolishing the existing buildings is
also in progress to move forward. The operators are also working on the back end completing
the logistics of the projects and are preparing the plans for plan check submittal.

Interim Vice-Chair Salas thanked staff for the hard work that is done to continue to move the City
forward.

Commissioner Moreno advised that he hopes to be a contributing member to the Planning
Commission.

Commissioner Covarrubias thanked staff and the Planning Commission for their support and
expressed gratitude for being involved with the City at this capacity.

Interim Chair Tamashiro also welcomed his new fellow Planning Commissioners to the body and
expressed his fulfillment on being apart of the Planning Commission and provided some
background on his experience being apart of the Planning Commission for the City.
